core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ali (عليّ, ʿAlī) is an Arabic masculine name associated with the root ع ل و (ʿ-l-w), whose semantic field includes height and elevation. It is commonly glossed as “high,” “exalted” or “sublime.” It is also borne by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and a major figure in early Islamic history.

faq.q: What does Ali mean in Arabic?
faq.a: Ali (عليّ, ʿAlī) is commonly glossed as “high,” “exalted” or “sublime.”

faq.q: What is the root of Ali?
faq.a: It is associated with the Arabic root ع ل و (ʿ-l-w), whose semantic field includes height and elevation.

faq.q: Who was Ali ibn Abi Talib?
faq.a: He was the Prophet Muhammad’s cousin and son-in-law and a central figure in early Islamic history.

faq.q: How is Ali viewed in Sunni and Shia traditions?
faq.a: Sunni Muslims recognise Ali as the fourth caliph; Shia Muslims regard him as the first Imam. Both traditions hold him in high esteem but differ on succession and authority.

faq.q: Is Ali a Qur’anic personal name?
faq.a: The Arabic word ʿaliyy and related forms occur in Qur’anic Arabic. That linguistic fact is distinct from identifying the proper name Ali as a person in a particular verse.

faq.q: What does Ali mean in Urdu?
faq.a: It is written علی and is commonly associated with بلند، عالی or برتر — high or exalted.
A practical English guide is “AH-lee”; pronunciation varies by language and region.

faq.q: Does Ali’s meaning describe a person’s character?
faq.a: No. “Exalted” is a lexical meaning, not evidence that a person has a particular personality or status.
